title: The 5 Longest Railway Tunnels on Earth, Ranked (#1 Isn't Under the Sea)

scenes.text: The longest railway tunnel on Earth isn't under the sea.

scenes.label: Shanghai Airport · 40.2 km
scenes.text: Number five: the Shanghai Airport tunnel in China. About forty kilometers long, and it opened only in 2024.

scenes.label: Yulhyeon · 50.3 km
scenes.text: Number four: the Yulhyeon Tunnel in South Korea. Fifty point three kilometers of high-speed track, opened in 2016.

scenes.label: Channel Tunnel · 50.5 km
scenes.text: Number three: the Channel Tunnel. About fifty and a half kilometers, linking England and France.

scenes.label: Seikan · 53.9 km
scenes.text: Number two: Japan's Seikan Tunnel. Nearly fifty-four kilometers long, with about twenty-three of them beneath the sea.

scenes.label: Gotthard Base · 57.1 km
scenes.text: Number one: the Gotthard Base Tunnel in Switzerland. Fifty-seven kilometers straight through the Alps, opened in 2016.

description:
The five longest railway tunnels in operation, ranked by length.
The record belongs to the Gotthard Base Tunnel in Switzerland at 57.1 kilometers, and it runs under mountains, not the sea.
Which tunnel would you ride through first?
first_comment: Would you ride under the sea or under the Alps? What should we rank next?
